novel_features.name: Config integrity audit
novel_features.description: Flag every ring group, queue, inbound/outbound rule, and IVR destination that points at a deleted, disabled, or non-existent extension or DID.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a cross-entity join across the whole config graph in local SQLite that no single XAPI call can return.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to catch broken call routing before users do, surfacing dangling references the 3CX console cannot detect.

novel_features.name: Config snapshot and diff
novel_features.description: Capture the full PBX config to a local snapshot, then show exactly what changed between two points in time or two tenants.
novel_features.rationale: The PBX has no concept of config history; only a local mirror of every entity makes row-level drift detection possible.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for change management, proving what changed, when, and by how much across the whole config.

novel_features.name: Bulk provision from CSV
novel_features.description: Idempotently create extensions and users from a CSV, assigning groups and roles, with a dry-run plan and typed exit codes.
novel_features.rationale: Turns hundreds of console clicks into one auditable, replayable command; the local plan and diff make it idempotent.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to onboard a whole tenant in one command instead of clicking the web console per extension.

novel_features.name: Queue and agent performance rollup
novel_features.description: One cross-queue table joining queue performance, agent-in-queue stats, abandoned calls, and SLA breaches over a time window.
novel_features.rationale: Joins four separate reporting endpoints into a single rollup the per-queue console screens never aggregate.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to compare queues and weeks at a glance instead of opening one slow report screen per queue.

novel_features.name: Offline directory search
novel_features.description: Instant full-text search across the mirrored config graph (users, groups, ring groups, queues, trunks, DIDs, contacts) by number, name, email, or extension.
novel_features.rationale: FTS5 over the local mirror answers lookups instantly without paging the live API across many collections.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when you know a number or name and need the object fast, across every entity type at once.

novel_features.name: Security posture report
novel_features.description: Consolidate blocklist, blacklisted numbers, anti-hacking settings, firewall state, failed-auth events, and the admin audit log into one attack-surface report.
novel_features.rationale: Aggregates several security and log endpoints the console scatters across separate screens into one report.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this for a one-shot security review instead of hunting across Security and Logs screens.

novel_features.name: Extension routing trace
novel_features.description: For one extension, show every inbound rule, ring group, queue, DID, and forwarding profile that routes to it.
novel_features.rationale: Walks the routing graph in local SQLite to answer reachability for a single DN; no single API call traverses these relations.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to answer why an extension is not ringing by seeing every path that reaches it.

novel_features.name: Live state merge
novel_features.description: A single time-windowed feed merging activity log, event log, active calls, and system status into the state of the PBX now or since a given time.
novel_features.rationale: Merges four live endpoints into one window-scoped view the console never combines.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this as the first command when triaging something wrong right now on a PBX.

narrative.headline: Every 3CX Configuration API (XAPI) object in one Go binary, with a local mirror of your whole PBX, offline search, config diffing, and cross-entity auditing no 3CX tool has.
narrative.value_prop: Covers the full 3CX V20+ Configuration API: users, groups, ring groups, queues, IVRs, trunks, DIDs, in/outbound rules, reporting, backups, security, and integrations. Beyond CRUD, it mirrors the entire config graph into local SQLite so you can search it offline, diff it over time, audit it for dangling references, roll up queue and agent performance, and trace exactly what routes to an extension.
narrative.auth_narrative: Authentication is OAuth2 client-credentials. Create an API client in the 3CX Web Client under Admin > Integrations > API, enable the 3CX Configuration API checkbox, and assign the Service Principal the System Owner role (System Administrator causes 403 on call history and several reports). Set TCX_CLIENT_ID and TCX_CLIENT_SECRET, and point the CLI at your instance with TCX_FQDN (or the base-url config). The CLI mints and caches a Bearer token from /connect/token and refreshes it automatically (tokens last 60 minutes).

quickstart.comment: Health check: confirms config and auth wiring before any live call.
Mirror the core config graph into local SQLite, the basis for search, audit, diff, and trace.
Find broken routing: destinations pointing at deleted or disabled objects.
Cross-queue performance and SLA rollup for the last week.

troubleshoots.symptom: 403 Forbidden on call history or reports
troubleshoots.fix: The API client Service Principal needs the System Owner role, not System Administrator. Re-assign it under Admin > Integrations > API.
Check TCX_CLIENT_ID and TCX_CLIENT_SECRET and that the API client has the 3CX Configuration API checkbox enabled. Run: 3cx-xapi-pp-cli doctor
Set TCX_FQDN (or the base-url config) to your instance, for example https://your-company.3cx.com.au; the CLI appends /xapi/v1 and /connect/token automatically.

troubleshoots.symptom: search, audit, or trace return nothing
troubleshoots.fix: Populate the local mirror first: 3cx-xapi-pp-cli sync --resources users,groups,ring-groups,queues,trunks,inbound-rules,did-numbers

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI to manage and reason about a 3CX V20+ phone system from scripts or an agent: provisioning extensions in bulk, auditing the config graph for broken routing, diffing config over time, rolling up queue and agent performance, and tracing how calls reach an extension. It is ideal when you want offline, queryable, agent-native access to a PBX whose web console is slow and siloed.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI for real-time call control (answer, transfer, or originate a live call); that is the separate 3CX Call Control API, not the Configuration API.
Do not use it to place or receive calls or as a softphone.
Do not use it for end-user voicemail playback or webclient chat; it manages configuration and reporting, not the user-facing client.
